records.summary: New source evidence checked on 7 October updates the earlier 6 October evidence-gap assessment below. The recovered Gabrani study supports a concern about out-of-pocket costs, but does not alone establish a direct contradiction of the WHO mental-health profile. Its December 2018 survey covers adults with several chronic conditions in Fier and Diber; the analysed group comprised 898 people who had consulted a provider in the preceding eight weeks. Table 2 distinguishes paying for all drugs (38%), at least one drug (49%) and receiving all drugs free (13%). Those mixed-condition results cannot be treated as a national percentage for mental-health patients or for the particular listed medicines. The reviewer’s criticism remains intact; the mental-health subgroup, WHO reporting basis and exemptions need further comparison. The reviewer cites Figure 1 for a proportion above 75%; that figure is a box plot of medicine expenditure by condition, and does not directly show the percentage paying for medication or consultations.
